podcast.title: Post-Nirvana Musical Ventures
podcast.body: After Kurt Cobain's death, Chris Novoselic attempted to continue his musical career with several bands, but none achieved significant success. "Chris Nova Selich, the guy everyone thought would be the person to carry on Nirvana's musical legacy, tried to keep things going with a couple of bands, but things just didn't work out."

podcast.title: Solo Album Rumors and Flipper Stint
podcast.body: Rumors of a Chris Novoselic solo album in 2005 were interrupted by a stint with the old-school punk band Flipper. He planned to record an album with Flipper, but in September 2008, he cancelled all tours and the album was never recorded due to his increasing responsibilities at home and involvement in regional politics. "There were rumblings of a Christian of a solid solo album in 2005, but that was interrupted by a stint with an old-school punk band called Flipper."

podcast.title: Speculated Post-Nirvana Life (if Kurt Lived)
podcast.body: It is speculated that if Kurt had lived and pursued an acoustic career, Chris Novoselic would have continued to follow his political interests, potentially sticking with Kurt to support him. "Chris Nova Selich. Well, he was always the activist of the band, the political guy. So as Dave went off with the food fighters and Kurt became this accoustic guy, I could still see Chris following his political interests."

xref.title: Informal Audition and Membership (1990)
xref.body: When Dave Grohl arrived in Seattle on September 21, 1990, to audition for Nirvana, Kurt Cobain and Chris Novoselic picked him up from the airport and drove to Chris's place where Dave was to stay. After hanging out and auditioning, Dave "just kind of became a member of the band" without a formal invitation or declaration. "No one said anything like, congratulations, you're in the group. They just didn't ask him to leave. So he stayed."

xref.title: 1992 MTV Music Video Awards Altercation
xref.body: The animosity between Nirvana and Guns N' Roses culminated in a backstage altercation at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards. Axl Rose confronted Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love, reportedly telling Kurt to "keep his woman in line." Simultaneously, Nirvana bassist Chris Novoselic and Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan were also arguing. "This boiled over to an altercation backstage at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards between Axel, Kurt and Courtney Love."

xref.title: Royalty Dispute Post-Nevermind (1992)
xref.body: In the spring of 1992, after *Nevermind* became a global success, Kurt Cobain decided to unilaterally rewrite the band's royalty arrangements. He demanded 90% of the songwriting royalties, backdated to *Nevermind*'s release in September 1991, and called Dave Grohl and Chris Novoselic "greedy" for wanting a larger cut. After "a bunch of fights," Kurt was eventually "bargained down to 75%" of all material on *Nevermind*. "Things got really heated, especially when Kurt called Dave and Chris Greedy for wanting a bigger cut."

xref.title: Death by Suicide (April 5, 1994)
xref.body: Kurt Cobain died in the early morning of Tuesday, April 5, 1994, by suicide via shotgun, preceded by a massive heroin overdose. His body was found approximately two weeks later, on April 8. His family and friends were aware he was in trouble, especially after a previous suicide attempt at a hotel in Rome. On March 25, 1994, an intervention was held at his Seattle home with his wife Courtney Love, bandmates Chris Novoselic and Dave Grohl, touring guitarist Pat Smear, and members of Nirvana's management and legal team, lasting five hours. He seemed convinced to seek help and flew to LA on March 30 to check into the Exodus Recovery Center. However, he left on April 1 (Good Friday) by scaling a six-foot wall, flew back to Seattle, and disappeared. His final note, addressed to his imaginary friend "Boddah," was found in his pocket after he injected a large amount of Mexican black tar heroin and then used a Remington shotgun to kill himself in the greenhouse at his home. "He had injected so much heroin that he probably never even heard the gun go off."

xref.title: Intervention Attempt (March 25, 1994)
xref.body: On March 25, 1994, Kurt Cobain's wife, Courtney Love, gathered a group of doctors and friends at their Seattle home for an intervention. The group included Courtney, Nirvana bandmates Chris Novoselic and Dave Grohl, touring Nirvana guitarist Pat Smear, and members of Nirvana's management and legal team. This intervention lasted for five hours and was an attempt to confront Kurt about his problems and convince him to seek help. "This intervention lasted for five hours. When it was all over, Kurt seemed convinced, and he flew to LA on the 30th to check into a rehab unit known for straightening out strong-out celebrities."

xref.title: Chris Novoselic's Family Move to Aberdeen
xref.body: Chris Novoselic was born in California, but his family relocated to Aberdeen when he was 14. They moved due to high property prices in California and the appeal of Aberdeen's Croatian community to Chris's father. Chris's dad became a machinist at a lumber mill, and his mother opened Maria's Hair Design beauty salon on South M Street. "Chris was born in California, but his family moved to Aberdeen when he was 14. Well why would they move there? Well property prices were too high in California, and besides Aberdeen had a lot of Croatian families, something that appealed to Chris's dad. He got a job as a machinist of one of the lumber mills and mum opened a beauty salon called Maria's Hair Design on South M Street."

xref.title: Krist Novoselic – Name History from Croatian Birth Spelling to English Variations
xref.body: Born May 16, 1965 to Croatian immigrant parents, Krist's birth name was spelled "Krste" in the Old World Croatian way (his father's name being Kristo). At school the name was Anglicized to "Chris" (C-H-R-I-S). At age 15 in 1980, he attended a Croatian high school in Zadar on the Adriatic coast, where classes included assembling and disassembling a machine gun as part of civil defense training. Returning to Aberdeen, he favored "Krist" (K-R-I-S-T) again. Early Nirvana materials often credited him as "Chris Novoselic" (likely a record company decision), but from *Nevermind* onward it has been "Krist." Anyone calling him "Chris" was corrected. "Novoselic was a fairly unusual name for Croatian and Serbian — it meant 'new villager.'"

xref.title: Steve Albini's Master Tapes Hostage Situation
xref.body: Producer Steve Albini had a deal stipulating no changes after his final mix. When the label wanted modifications to *In Utero*, he refused to hand over the master tapes, "essentially holding them hostage," until bassist Chris Novoselic convinced him to comply. "He even refused to hand over the master tapes for a while, essentially holding them hostage."
